provenance.note: Held-out family implementing the four evidence situations summarized in Module 03 Section 4.2.

cases.task: Define what a source baseline identifies.
cases.supplied_source: The evaluation packet contains a review source. Its source baseline points to that source so that a proposal can be checked against it.
cases.mutation_note: Course-authored held-out case (H1, Module 03 Table 4.1) using a distinct source passage for the source-baseline concept.

cases.task: Define what a source baseline identifies.
cases.supplied_source: The evaluation packet contains a review source. Its source baseline points to that source so that a proposal can be checked against it. In the separate equipment-maintenance process, a supervisor approves replacement requests.
cases.mutation_note: Course-authored held-out case (H2, Module 03 Table 4.1): the equipment-maintenance supervisor is a distractor that must not be attached to the baseline concept.

cases.task: State the retention duration of the review records named in this packet.
cases.supplied_source: The evaluation packet contains a review source and review records. Each record contains the source identifier and the review decision.
cases.mutation_note: Course-authored held-out case (H3, Module 03 Table 4.1) reworded into the evaluation-packet scenario; retention duration is absent.

cases.task: Describe the scope of the source baseline recorded in this note.
cases.supplied_source: The materials prepared for review include a source excerpt and a snapshot of the entire repository. The reviewer records a baseline before reviewing the proposal. This note does not specify which of the two objects the baseline identifies.
cases.mutation_note: Course-authored held-out case (H4, Module 03 Table 4.1): the note explicitly states the ambiguity that must remain unresolved.

expected_behaviors.expected_behavior: A supported response preserves the relation between the baseline and the review source used to check a proposal. 'Identifies material' alone omits the checking relationship.
A supported response preserves the checking relationship and does not attach the equipment-maintenance supervisor or approval authority to the source baseline.
The source names no retention duration, so a supported response states that the duration is not specified instead of inventing one.
The note states that it does not specify which stored object the baseline identifies, so a supported response reports that unresolved scope rather than choosing the excerpt or the snapshot.
